2608.25852v1 Switching of Ground State Composition in a Bilayer— Even though the quality factor study has shown advantages of the Light-Hole ground state, we design a further heterostructure where the strengths of both HH and LH ground states are utilized, exploiting the opportunities offered by lattice-matching tensile ε \varepsilon -SiGe barriers to a Ge substrate.
Building on the demonstrated architecture of ε \varepsilon -Ge bilayer [ 28 ] and the concurrent switchable HH-LH proposal [ 12 ] , here we propose to stack a tensile ε \varepsilon -SiGe quantum well on top of a Ge channel [ 5 ] with a ε \varepsilon -SiGe barrier in-between. Specifically, the bottom 18 18 nm Ge well is cladded by tensile ε \varepsilon -Si 0.12 Ge 0.88 , with the thin top barrier also acting as intra-well spacer. The top 15 15 nm quantum well is tensile ε \varepsilon -Si 0.05 Ge 0.95 , with a top ε \varepsilon -Si 0.3 Ge 0.7 barrier separating the bilayer from the surface. As shown in Fig. 4 c-d), this bilayer stack allows switching the ground state composition between HH and LH by simply changing the applied voltage on the top plunger gate, modeled here via a linear out-of-plane electric field. Fig. 4 e) shows the computed linear SOC α \alpha as a function of the vertical electric field and displays a three orders of magnitude increase exactly where the ground state switches from HH to LH character. Similarly in Fig. 4 f) we extract the planar and out-of-plane g-factor and see the same discontinuous jump from typical HH behaviour with g ⟂ ∗ > g ∥ ∗ g_{\perp}^{*}>g^{*}_{\parallel} to the LH inverted setup. In practice, such a heterostructure allows us to exploit the fast operation capabilities of the LH layer while still being able to access the HH ground state.
